item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Sun Oct 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico, and on newly formed Tropical Depression Three-C, located
several hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Three-C are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Three-C are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Olana (CP3/CP032026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...DEPRESSION BECOMES TROPICAL STORM OLANA... As of 11:00 AM HST Sun Oct 25 the center of Olana was located near 14.8, -178.0 with movement ENE at 8 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1002 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Public Advisory Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPA33 PHFO 252034
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Olana Advisory Number   2
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
...DEPRESSION BECOMES TROPICAL STORM OLANA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.8N 178.0W
ABOUT 580 MI...935 KM WSW OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 75 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Johnston Atoll should monitor the progress of this
system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Olana was
located near latitude 14.8 North, longitude 178.0 West. Olana is
moving toward the east-northeast near 8 mph (13 km/h) and a general
eastward motion is expected for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with
higher gusts. Some slight intensification is possible later today,
but weakening is forecast to begin on Monday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 252035
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Olana Discussion Number   2
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Oct 25 2026

Since the prior advisory, convective activity has continued to 
expand near and to the northeast of the estimated center of the 
tropical cyclone, with first light visible imagery indicating that 
the center is likely embedded in this mass of deep convection. A 
helpful WSF-M pass at 18 UTC also showed further organization, with 
a curved band on its northwest flank, though some northeast tilt 
with height is also noted between the 37 GHz and 89 GHz channels. 
The latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimates were T1.5/25 kt 
from JTWC and T2.0/30 kt from HFO. However, the objective intensity 
estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 30-36 kt, and given the 
improvement seen on satellite and microwave imagery since the prior 
advisory, the initial intensity is set on the higher side of the 
intensity estimates at 35 kt, making the depression Tropical Storm 
Olana.
 
Olana is estimated to be moving a bit faster to the east-northeast 
this morning, or 075/7 kt. The track reasoning is the same as this 
morning, with the combination of a low-level westerly wind burst to 
the south and a mid-latitude trough to the northwest expected to 
maintain the tropical storm on a general eastward track. The track 
guidance this cycle has shifted slower compared to the previous 
advisory, as the circulation becomes more vertically shallow, and 
the NHC track was also made slower than the previous forecast. The 
latest track forecast is on the northern side of the guidance 
envelope, favoring a blend of the faster HFIP Corrected Consensus 
Approach (HCCA) and slower ECMWF (EMXI) track guidance. Based on the 
latest track forecast, no watches are required for Johnston Atoll at 
this time, though interests there should continue to monitor the 
latest forecast updates related to this system.
 
There remains a small window for Olana to intensify a bit more in 
the short-term given its current structure, though the noted tilt 
with height seen on the WSF-M microwave pass is likely a harbinger 
of stronger vertical wind shear that the tropical cyclone will soon 
begin to experience. While both the GFS and EC-based SHIPS guidance 
are only forecasting 10-15 kt of deep-layer (200-850 mb) westerly 
shear over the next 12-36 h, the adjusted shear is much higher, 
suggesting higher shear undercutting the outflow layer. Weakening is 
expected to begin in 12-24 h, and this will likely be hastened when 
the deep-layer shear increases above 30 kt in 48-60 h. Both the GFS 
and ECMWF simulated IR show the remaining convection being fully 
stripped away from Olana's circulation during this period. Thus, the 
NHC intensity forecast shows Olana becoming a remnant low by 60 h, 
with the low opening up into a trough after 72 h, though the global 
models suggest the circulation could become too elongated to be 
considered well-defined earlier than shown here. 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/2100Z 14.8N 178.0W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  26/0600Z 14.9N 177.2W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  26/1800Z 14.4N 176.2W   35 KT  40 MPH
 36H  27/0600Z 14.1N 175.3W   35 KT  40 MPH
